memory_update.text: PWR is the reference leader for the grid EPC labor and utility field-services node, but its mega-cap size and high attention make it more useful as a benchmark than an underfollowed discovery target.
MYRG is a strong underfollowed candidate for T&D specialty electrical construction exposure, especially if filings confirm durable T&D backlog, utility MSAs, and margin stability.

PRIM is a plausible underfollowed grid-services candidate through its Utilities/Power Delivery business, but later layers should separate power delivery from broader construction and gas utility exposure.
NVEE is a lower-attention testing/inspection/geospatial/utility-services hypothesis for the monitoring and commissioning side of the node; exposure purity needs verification before promotion.

Layer 1B found fewer pure-play public testing, protection-relay commissioning, drone inspection, and utility field-service companies than EPC contractors; many direct operators may be private, embedded in larger engineering firms, or hidden inside consulting/testing conglomerates.
Use PWR as the reference comp for grid EPC and electric infrastructure field-service demand, but avoid letting it crowd out smaller discovery candidates.
MYRG is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for this node because its T&D segment directly maps to transmission, distribution, substations, and utility electrical construction services.
PRIM is a second-order grid-services candidate; require segment-level proof that power delivery is material enough to offset broader gas, communications, pipeline, and renewables mix.

TIC is a newly rebranded inspection/testing/geospatial platform worth tracking for utility asset integrity and grid monitoring, but utility-grid revenue exposure must be verified before promotion beyond hypothesis.

For grid EPC labor and testing services, the key survival evidence should include backlog duration, utility customer concentration, labor/safety metrics, fixed-price exposure, project closeout volatility, and margins under skilled-labor scarcity.

Need a follow-up search for smaller pure-play substation testing, protection relay testing, drone/robotic inspection, utility vegetation management, and commissioning companies; many may be private, acquired, or hidden inside diversified service firms.

MYRG should be tracked as a smaller public specialty electrical contractor with explicit T&D segment exposure and backlog disclosure; key verification is whether backlog quality and margins improve with grid modernization demand.

PRIM should be tracked as an underfollowed diversified infrastructure contractor with direct power delivery and utility maintenance exposure; isolate Utilities/Power Delivery from broader renewables, pipeline, and civil work.

NVEE is a lower-confidence testing/inspection/commissioning candidate; keep only if filings confirm material utility, power delivery, substation, data-center commissioning, or grid reliability service revenue.

For this node, backlog alone is insufficient: later layers should verify scarce labor availability, safety performance, customer concentration, storm-restoration mix, outage-window scheduling, fixed-price contract risk, and margin stability.

Public pure-plays in relay testing, substation commissioning, drone/robotic line inspection, and utility asset inspection appear scarce; later searches should look for hidden exposure inside engineering roll-ups, geospatial software firms, and small-cap inspection/testing companies.

MYRG should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a direct mid-cap grid EPC and T&D electrical-construction candidate; next layers should test backlog quality, T&D margin stability, safety metrics, labor availability, and utility customer exposure.

PRIM should remain in the underfollowed lane but with a purity discount because power delivery is embedded inside a broader specialty-construction platform exposed to renewables, gas, pipeline, industrial, and storm-restoration volatility.

TIC is a useful inspection/monitoring/geospatial-services hypothesis after the Acuren-NV5 merger, but it requires post-merger segment evidence before being treated as a clean grid-services beneficiary.

For this node, the most relevant underfollowed signals are not equipment orders alone but field labor availability, T&D backlog conversion, safety record, storm-restoration demand, outage coordination, commissioning capability, inspection/vegetation-management contracts, and utility qualification barriers.

Need a dedicated follow-up search for smaller US-listed drone, LiDAR, vegetation-management, relay-testing, and substation-commissioning providers; many may be private, acquired, or hidden inside engineering/TICC platforms.

node: Grid EPC labor, utility field services, testing, inspection, monitoring, and commissioning
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B universe expansion for the grid EPC labor and utility field-services node identifies Quanta Services as the high-attention reference leader, with MYR Group, Primoris Services, and NV5 Global as more underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery candidates. The common chokepoint is not just grid capex, but the ability to deploy skilled crews, substation/transmission/distribution construction capacity, maintenance, inspection, testing, and project execution services needed to turn equipment orders into energized infrastructure. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. This pass expands the universe around labor-intensive grid execution and asset-integrity services. The reference lane is Quanta Services, which validates the demand and backlog signal for electric grid services. The underfollowed lane emphasizes smaller or less thematically crowded US-listed companies with transmission/distribution construction, utility maintenance, power delivery, testing, inspection, certification, geospatial, and commissioning exposure. Key chokepoint logic: grid capex does not become energized infrastructure without specialized crews, substation/transmission execution, outage coordination, inspection, and commissioning. Evidence is strongest for PWR, MYRG, PRIM, and TIC as direct or adjacent node participants; margin durability, backlog conversion, safety performance, labor availability, and utility customer concentration remain the next evidence gates.
